misconception.description: reaching a target margin by adding that percentage to the cost, which applies it to the cost rather than to the selling price

worked_example.text: A bookshop buys a hardback for EUR 45 and wants a gross margin of 40% of the selling price.
worked_example.solution: If the margin takes 40% of the price, the cost is the other 60%: price = 45 / 0.6 = EUR 75. Check: the profit is 75 - 45 = EUR 30, which is 40% of 75. Adding 40% to the cost would have given EUR 63, where the profit of EUR 18 is only 28.6% of the price.

problem.text: A boutique buys a jacket for EUR 84 and wants a gross margin of 30% of the selling price. What price should it set?

distractors.note: the documented misconception: 30% added to the cost, which is a markup and not a margin
dividing by the margin rather than by one minus the margin

hints: Decide first what the 30% is a percentage of. A gross margin is always measured against the selling price, never against what the boutique paid.
If three tenths of the price is to be gross profit, then seven tenths of it is the EUR 84 the jacket cost. Write that as an equation before rearranging it.
Divide the cost by one minus the target margin, then check your answer by dividing the profit by the price you set.
worked_solution: Step 1: read the percentage against the right base. The margin is a share of the selling price, so the cost must be 1 - 0.3 = 0.7 of it. Step 2: write the relationship: 84 = price x 0.7. Step 3: divide: 84 / 0.7 = EUR 120.00. Check it: the gross profit is 120 - 84 = EUR 36, and 36 / 120 is 30% of the price, exactly as required. Adding 30% to the cost would give EUR 109.20, where the profit of EUR 25.20 is only 23.1% of the price, because the percentage was applied to the smaller of the two bases.

near_transfer.text: The same boutique buys a coat for EUR 126 and wants a gross margin of 25% of the selling price on it. What price should it set?

distractors.note: the misconception: a markup on cost instead of a margin on price
dividing by the margin instead of by one minus the margin

far_transfer.text: A wholesaler prices its goods by adding a 25% markup to what they cost. What gross margin on the selling price does that produce?

distractors.note: treating a markup on cost and a margin on price as the same number
reading the margin as whatever the markup leaves over
